📝 Practice MCQs 10 Questions
1The MOST IMPORTANT histological feature distinguishing large intestine from small intestine:
✅ Show Answer
✅ A — The large intestine has NO VILLI and NO plicae circulares — only deep straight crypts. This is the most important distinguishing histological feature.
2Taeniae coli are formed by:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Taeniae coli = 3 thickened bands of the OUTER LONGITUDINAL layer of muscularis externa → they are shorter than the bowel wall → remaining wall sacculates → haustra.
3Fat-filled serosal pouches of the large intestine are called:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Appendices epiploicae = fat-filled pouches in the connective tissue of the SEROSA of the large intestine. They are absent in the small intestine.
4Which cells are ABSENT in the large intestine but PRESENT in the small intestine crypts?
✅ Show Answer
✅ D — Paneth cells are found ONLY in the crypts of the SMALL INTESTINE. They are ABSENT in the large intestine.
5Large intestinal submucosa differs from duodenal submucosa by:
✅ Show Answer
✅ D — Large intestinal submucosa LACKS submucosal glands. Brunner's glands are exclusive to the DUODENAL submucosa.
6Goblet cells in the large intestine INCREASE from:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Goblet cells increase in number from cecum → sigmoid colon. The more distal the colon, the more solid the content → more mucus needed for lubrication.
7Haustra (sacculations) of the colon are caused by:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Taeniae coli are shorter than the total length of the colon wall → the segments of wall between the 3 bands bulge outward → haustra (sacculations).
8Bacterial flora in the large intestine produce:
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — Colonic bacterial flora synthesize: Vitamin K (essential for clotting factors), Vitamin B12, riboflavin (B2), and thiamin (B1). Antibiotics kill flora → potential K and B-vitamin deficiency.
9The large intestine has NO Peyer's patches because:
✅ Show Answer
✅ A — Peyer's patches (aggregated lymphoid nodules) are found ONLY in the ILEUM. The large intestine has solitary lymphoid nodules in lamina propria only.
10Auerbach's (myenteric) plexus in large intestine is located:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Auerbach's plexus is located BETWEEN the inner circular and outer longitudinal layers of muscularis externa — same location as in small intestine. It controls motor activity.
3Exocrine Portion of Pancreas›

Overview — Pancreas as a Mixed Gland

  • The pancreas is a MIXED GLAND:
  • → Exocrine portion (acini + duct system) — digestive enzymes + alkaline juice
  • → Endocrine portion (Islets of Langerhans) — hormones
  • Exocrine type: Compound tubuloacinar SEROUS gland (similar to parotid gland in structure)

Stroma

  • Capsule: Poorly developed, THIN connective tissue capsule
  • Septa: Thin septa arise from capsule → divide gland into LOBES and LOBULES
  • Reticular CT: Forms the delicate framework supporting the parenchyma

Parenchyma — Acinar Cells (Detailed LM & EM)

  • Shape: Pyramidal cells arranged in ACINI (round/oval clusters)
  • LM features:
  • → Basal nucleus (round, basal)
  • → Basal cytoplasm: BASOPHILIC (abundant RER for protein synthesis)
  • → Apical cytoplasm: ACIDOPHILIC due to ZYMOGEN GRANULES (contain inactive proenzymes)
  • EM (Ultrastructural) features — TYPICAL PROTEIN-SECRETING CELL:
  • → Abundant BASAL RER (protein synthesis)
  • → Many MITOCHONDRIA
  • → Prominent SUPRANUCLEAR GOLGI APPARATUS (protein processing and packaging)
  • → Large membrane-bound ELECTRON-DENSE apical zymogen granules
  • Lateral borders: Joined by JUNCTIONAL COMPLEXES:
  • → Protect cells from separation
  • → TIGHT JUNCTIONS prevent enzymes discharged into lumen from reaching intercellular space (prevents local autodigestion)

Duct System — 5 Levels (Unique Feature)

  • Level 1 — Centroacinar cells (UNIQUE TO PANCREAS):
  • → Pale SQUAMOUS or low CUBOIDAL cells
  • → Constitute the INTRA-ACINAR portion of the intercalated duct
  • → Found ONLY in pancreatic acini — NOT in parotid or other glands
  • → KEY HISTOLOGICAL DISTINGUISHING FEATURE between pancreas and parotid
  • Level 2 — Intercalated ducts: Lined with LOW CUBOIDAL cells
  • Level 3 — Intralobular ducts: Very small ducts
  • Level 4 — Interlobular ducts: More prominent; lined by SIMPLE LOW COLUMNAR epithelium
  • Level 5 — Main duct (Duct of Wirsung): Lined by SIMPLE COLUMNAR epithelium; joins CBD → ampulla of Vater → sphincter of Oddi → 2nd part of duodenum

Functions of Exocrine Portion

  • 1. Secretion of ALKALINE WATERY SECRETION (HCO₃⁻-rich from duct cells) → neutralizes acidic chyme from stomach → protects duodenal mucosa
  • 2. Secretion of ENZYMES AND PROENZYMES:
  • → Trypsinogen (→ trypsin by enterokinase)
  • → Chymotrypsinogen (→ chymotrypsin by trypsin)
  • → Proelastase (→ elastase)
  • → Lipase (active)
  • → Phospholipase
  • → Amylase (active)
📝 Practice MCQs 10 Questions
1Centroacinar cells are found ONLY in which gland?
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Centroacinar cells (pale, low cuboidal/squamous) constitute the intra-acinar portion of the intercalated duct and are found ONLY in PANCREATIC ACINI — the key histological feature distinguishing pancreas from parotid.
2The APICAL cytoplasm of pancreatic acinar cells is acidophilic because of:
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — Zymogen granules (containing inactive proenzymes like trypsinogen, chymotrypsinogen) in the APICAL cytoplasm are ACIDOPHILIC (eosinophilic/red on H&E). The BASAL cytoplasm is BASOPHILIC (due to abundant RER).
3Beta (β) cells of the islets of Langerhans:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — β cells: ~70% of islet cells; located in the CENTER; irregular granules with wide electron-lucent region; synthesize proinsulin → secrete insulin → ↓ blood glucose.
4Somatostatin from δ (delta) cells:
✅ Show Answer
✅ D — δ cells secrete somatostatin → paracrine inhibition of α cells (↓ glucagon) AND β cells (↓ insulin) + ↓ intestinal motility.
5The main duct of the pancreas (Duct of Wirsung) is lined by:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Main pancreatic duct (Duct of Wirsung) = SIMPLE COLUMNAR epithelium. Intercalated ducts = low cuboidal. Centroacinar cells = squamous/low cuboidal.
6Tight junctions between acinar cell lateral borders prevent:
✅ Show Answer
✅ A — Tight junctions on lateral borders of acinar cells prevent digestive enzymes (once secreted into the lumen) from leaking into the intercellular space → prevents local autodigestion.
7PP (Pancreatic Polypeptide) cells primarily:
✅ Show Answer
✅ D — PP (F) cells secrete pancreatic polypeptide → INHIBITS exocrine pancreatic secretion. They are very few in number.
8Exocrine pancreas is classified histologically as:
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — Exocrine pancreas = compound tubuloacinar SEROUS gland, same classification as the parotid gland. The distinguishing feature is the CENTROACINAR CELLS (unique to pancreas).
9Alpha (α) cells of islets release glucagon when:
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — α cells are at the PERIPHERY of islets; they respond to LOW blood glucose → secrete glucagon → acts on liver → glycogenolysis → ↑ blood glucose.
10Which of the following is a typical ultrastructural feature of pancreatic acinar cells as PROTEIN-SECRETING CELLS?
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Pancreatic acinar cells show ALL features of protein-secreting cells: basal RER (synthesis), many mitochondria (energy), prominent supranuclear Golgi (packaging), and large apical zymogen granules (storage + secretion).
4Liver›

Overview

  • The liver is the most important metabolic organ where absorbed nutrients are processed and stored
  • Dual function of the SAME CELL (hepatocyte):
  • → EXOCRINE: secretes bile (compound tubuloalveolar exocrine gland)
  • → ENDOCRINE: secretes hormones and plasma proteins

Stroma — Connective Tissue Framework

  • 1. Glisson's capsule:
  • → Thin CT capsule covering external surface of liver
  • → THICKENED at the HILUM (porta hepatis) where blood vessels and lymphatics enter/leave
  • → PARTIALLY covered by peritoneum (bare area has no peritoneal covering)
  • 2. Trabeculae:
  • → Arise from capsule → divide liver into lobes and lobules
  • → In HUMAN liver: interlobular CT is very THIN and INCOMPLETE → INDISTINCT lobulation
  • → In PIG liver: trabeculae are well-developed → distinct lobulation (why pig liver is used as teaching model)
  • 3. Reticular formation: Delicate framework to support liver parenchyma

Parenchyma — Hepatocytes (Light Microscopy)

  • Arrangement: Anastomosing cords (plates) of hepatocytes of TWO-CELL THICKNESS radiating from central veins like spokes of a wheel
  • Blood sinusoids: Enclosed between cell cords → lined mainly with endothelial cells + Kupffer cells
  • Shape and Size: Polyhedral (6+ surfaces); 20-30 μm diameter
  • Nucleus: Usually single, rounded, centrally located; about 25% of cells have TWO NUCLEI (binucleate); mitotic figures can be seen
  • Cytoplasm: ACIDOPHILIC (due to many mitochondria + SER); PAS-positive for glycogen; lipid vacuoles variable

Hepatocytes — Electron Microscopy

  • Nucleus: Euchromatic with peripheral heterochromatin clumps + 1-2 nucleoli
  • Cytoplasm contains:
  • 1. Abundant RER (protein synthesis — albumin, clotting factors)
  • 2. Numerous MITOCHONDRIA (energy production)
  • 3. Well-developed SER (DETOXIFICATION of drugs + steroids + carbohydrate metabolism)
  • 4. Well-developed GOLGI complexes (lipoproteins, glycoproteins processing)
  • 5. Numerous LYSOSOMES (digest and eliminate cellular waste)
  • 6. Free ribosomes scattered in cytoplasm
  • 7. PEROXISOMES: numerous; responsible for H₂O₂, lipid, and ALCOHOL degradation
  • 8. Intermediate filaments (cytokeratin) + actin filaments
  • 9. Cell inclusions: lipid droplets + GLYCOGEN granules

Hepatocyte Cell Membrane — Three Surfaces

  • Each hepatocyte surface is either:
  • 1. In contact with ANOTHER HEPATOCYTE
  • 2. In contact with BLOOD SINUSOIDS — through Space of Disse; these surfaces have MICROVILLI
  • 3. Sharing in formation of BILE CANALICULUS WALL — these surfaces also have microvilli; junctional complexes seal the canalicular lumen
  • Note: Sinusoidal and bile canalicular surfaces have microvilli; other surfaces (facing adjacent hepatocytes) LACK microvilli

Space of Disse — Detailed Contents

  • Definition: Space between endothelial cells lining blood sinusoids and the hepatocytes
  • Contents:
  • 1. BLOOD PLASMA (hepatocytes are directly bathed in plasma)
  • 2. MICROVILLI of hepatocytes (project into this space)
  • 3. RETICULAR FIBRES (support the sinusoidal wall)
  • 4. ITO CELLS (Fat-storing / Hepatic Stellate Cells):
  • → Support the blood sinusoid wall
  • → STORE VITAMIN A (largest vitamin A store in body)
  • → Secrete cytokines and growth factors
  • → In liver fibrosis/cirrhosis: ACTIVATED → become MYOFIBROBLASTS → secrete collagen → fibrosis
  • 5. Unmyelinated nerve fibres
  • 6. PIT CELLS (cells with short pseudopodia): NATURAL KILLER CELLS — provide hepatic innate immunity
  • Function of Space of Disse: Prevents collapse of sinusoidal wall; acts as intermediate compartment between hepatocytes and blood stream; facilitates metabolite exchange

Kupffer Cells

  • Found in wall of blood sinusoids — between or on the LUMINAL SURFACE of endothelial cells
  • TYPE: Phagocytic cell = resident macrophage of liver (part of mononuclear phagocytic system)
  • Demonstrated by TRYPAN BLUE stain (vital stain)
  • Functions:
  • 1. Metabolize AGED ERYTHROCYTES (break down RBCs)
  • 2. DIGEST HAEMOGLOBIN (→ bilirubin)
  • 3. Remove bacteria from portal blood
  • 4. Secrete proteins related to IMMUNOLOGIC processes (cytokines, complement components)

Hepatic Blood Sinusoids

  • Sinusoidal capillaries: irregularly dilated vessels between plates of liver lobule → drain into central vein
  • Wall: Discontinuous layer of FENESTRATED endothelial cells (with large pores/gaps) + supported by delicate reticular fibres
  • Also contain: Kupffer cells (phagocytic) + Pit cells (NK cells)
  • Blood flow: FROM portal area (periphery) → TOWARDS central vein (centripetal)

Bile Canaliculi & Bile Flow

  • Bile canaliculi: First portions of bile duct system
  • → 1-2 μm diameter TUBULES limited by plasma membranes of TWO ADJACENT HEPATOCYTES + their tight junctions
  • → Lateral surface has small number of microvilli
  • → Form anastomosing network
  • BILE FLOW DIRECTION: OPPOSITE to blood flow
  • → Blood: portal area (periphery) → central vein (CENTRIPETAL)
  • → Bile: central vein area → bile ductules → portal area (CENTRIFUGAL)
  • Bile duct system (order):
  • 1. Bile canaliculi (between hepatocytes)
  • 2. Bile ductules / Canals of Herring (lined by cuboidal cells at periphery of lobule)
  • 3. Bile ducts in portal area (cuboidal or columnar cells)
  • 4. Hepatic ducts R & L (simple cuboidal → simple columnar)
  • 5. Common hepatic duct (simple columnar + surrounding CT + smooth muscle)
  • 6. Cystic duct (from gallbladder)
  • 7. Common bile duct (columnar epithelium)
  • 8. Opens into duodenum at Sphincter of Oddi

Portal Area (Portal Tract / Canal)

  • Triangular area demarcated by CT at CORNERS of three adjacent hepatic lobules
  • Contents (Portal Triad):
  • → Branch of PORTAL VEIN
  • → Branch of HEPATIC ARTERY
  • → BILE DUCT
  • → Some nerves + lymphatics
  • Function: Drains bile to bile duct at its centre; supplies blood to sinusoids

Organisation of Liver — Three Models

  • 1. CLASSIC HEXAGONAL HEPATIC LOBULE (most common teaching model):
  • → Hexagonal mass of hepatocytes
  • → PORTAL TRACT at 6 CORNERS
  • → CENTRAL VEIN at the CENTER
  • → Plates of hepatocytes radiate from central vein
  • → Blood flows CENTRIPETALLY (portal area → central vein)
  • → Bile flows CENTRIFUGALLY (central area → portal tract)
  • → In human: CT septa between lobules are INDISTINCT
  • 2. PORTAL LOBULE:
  • → Triangular mass of hepatocytes
  • → PORTAL TRACT at the CENTER (bile duct = central)
  • → THREE CENTRAL VEINS at the corners
  • → Blood flows CENTRIFUGALLY (from hepatic artery outward)
  • → Bile flows CENTRIPETALLY toward portal tract (centre)
  • → This model considers liver as EXOCRINE GLAND (bile secretion)
  • 3. HEPATIC ACINUS (Rappaport — most physiologically meaningful):
  • → Diamond-shaped mass of hepatocytes
  • → Terminal branches of HEPATIC ARTERY at the CENTRE
  • → Formed of parts of TWO ADJACENT classical hepatic lobules
  • → Divided into 3 zones based on BLOOD SUPPLY:
  • Zone I (periportal) — closest to vascular core → RICHEST blood supply → first to receive O₂ + glucose → most active metabolism; MOST AFFECTED by viral hepatitis and phosphorus toxicity
  • Zone II (midzonal) — intermediate
  • Zone III (centrilobular/perivenous) — furthest from vascular core → POOREST blood supply → receives least O₂ → MOST VULNERABLE to ischaemia + toxic injury
⚠️ Zone III (centrilobular) is MOST VULNERABLE to: ischaemia (right heart failure → nutmeg liver), CCl₄ toxicity, PARACETAMOL overdose (NAPQI accumulates here — zone 3 necrosis), alcohol. Zone I is most affected by: viral hepatitis, yellow phosphorus toxicity.
📝 Practice MCQs 10 Questions
1Kupffer cells in the liver are:
✅ Show Answer
✅ D — Kupffer cells are the liver's RESIDENT MACROPHAGES (mononuclear phagocytic system), found lining the sinusoids. They phagocytose aged RBCs, bacteria from portal blood, and secrete immunological proteins.
2Bile flow direction in relation to blood flow:
✅ Show Answer
✅ D — Blood flows CENTRIPETALLY (portal area → central vein). Bile flows CENTRIFUGALLY (from bile canaliculi near central vein → bile ductules → portal area bile duct). They flow in OPPOSITE directions.
3The Space of Disse contains which cells that store vitamin A?
✅ Show Answer
✅ D — Ito cells (hepatic stellate/fat-storing cells) in the Space of Disse store vitamin A. When activated (e.g., in chronic liver injury), they become myofibroblasts → secrete collagen → liver fibrosis/cirrhosis.
4Zone III of the hepatic acinus (Rappaport) is MOST VULNERABLE because:
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — Zone III (centrilobular/perivenous) is POOREST in blood supply → lowest oxygen → most vulnerable to: ischaemia (heart failure), paracetamol toxicity (NAPQI accumulates here), CCl₄, alcohol.
5Glisson's capsule is:
✅ Show Answer
✅ A — Glisson's capsule: thin CT capsule covering the liver externally; thickened at the hilum (porta hepatis); partially covered by peritoneum (bare area lacks peritoneal covering).
6The portal triad contains:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Portal triad = portal area contains: branch of portal vein + branch of hepatic artery + bile duct (+ nerves and lymphatics). Found at the CORNERS of the classic hexagonal lobule.
7Hepatocyte plates in the liver are of what thickness?
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Hepatocyte cords/plates are TWO-CELL THICK (unlike gut epithelium which is one cell thick). They radiate from the central vein like spokes of a wheel, with sinusoids between the plates.
8Bile canaliculi are formed by:
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — Bile canaliculi are NOT true ducts with lining cells. They are the spaces formed between the opposing lateral membranes of two adjacent hepatocytes, sealed by tight junctions.
9In the classic hepatic lobule, the central vein is:
✅ Show Answer
✅ A — Classic hexagonal lobule: CENTRAL VEIN at the CENTER; portal triads at the 6 CORNERS. Hepatocyte plates radiate centrifugally from central vein; blood flows centripetally toward central vein.
10Human liver lobulation is INDISTINCT compared to pig liver because:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — In humans, the interlobular connective tissue septa are very thin and incomplete → lobule borders are NOT clearly visible on histological sections. In pigs, thick trabeculae make the hexagonal lobules clearly visible.

📝 Practice MCQs 60 Questions
1The epithelium covering intestinal villi mainly consists of:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Villi are lined by simple columnar epithelium made up of absorptive enterocytes interspersed with goblet cells.
2Plicae circularis are formed by:
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — Plicae circulares (valves of Kerckring) are permanent folds formed by the mucosa together with part of the submucosa, unlike villi which involve mucosa alone.
3Peyer's patches are mainly found in the:
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — Large aggregated lymphoid nodules (Peyer's patches) are characteristically abundant in the ileum, on its antimesenteric border.
4The central lymphatic vessel inside the villus is called:
✅ Show Answer
✅ A — Each villus contains a single blind-ended central lymphatic capillary called the lacteal, which absorbs chylomicrons.
5Paneth cells secrete:
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — Paneth cells, found at the base of intestinal crypts, secrete lysozyme and defensins that help control the gut bacterial population.
6Which of the following structures contributes MOST to the 30-fold increase in absorptive surface area?
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — Microvilli forming the brush border contribute the largest multiplication of surface area, more than plicae or villi alone.
7The actin filaments within microvilli are attached at their bases to:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — The core actin bundles of each microvillus insert into the terminal web, a meshwork of actin filaments just beneath the apical membrane.
8Which junction prevents paracellular leakage of intestinal contents?
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — The zonula occludens (tight junction) near the apex of enterocytes seals the intercellular space and prevents paracellular leakage.
9A histological section shows intestinal mucosa with broad leaf-shaped villi and Brunner's glands in submucosa. The section is from:
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — Brunner's glands in the submucosa, together with broad leaf/finger-shaped villi, are diagnostic of the duodenum.
10Peyer's patches penetrate through:
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — The large lymphoid nodules of Peyer's patches extend from the lamina propria through the muscularis mucosae into the submucosa.
11The upper half of the crypt of Lieberkühn is lined mainly by:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — The upper part of the crypt continues into the villus lining and is dominated by absorptive (columnar) cells and goblet cells, while Paneth and stem cells occupy the crypt base.
12Which enteroendocrine cell increases peristaltic movement?
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Enterochromaffin (EC) cells secrete serotonin (5-HT), which stimulates intestinal motility and peristalsis.
13A tumor destroying Paneth cells would MOST likely lead to:
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — Since Paneth cells secrete antimicrobial lysozyme and defensins that help regulate crypt flora, their loss favors bacterial overgrowth.
14Which of the following is NOT found in the lower half of intestinal crypts?
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — Mature absorptive enterocytes are found higher up toward the crypt-villus junction; the crypt base is dominated by stem cells, Paneth cells, and enteroendocrine cells.
15The central core of an intestinal villus contains ALL EXCEPT:
✅ Show Answer
✅ D — The villus core (lamina propria) contains a lacteal, capillary network, and scattered smooth muscle fibers, but the myenteric plexus lies between the muscle layers of the muscularis externa, not within the villus.
16M cells differ from enterocytes because they:
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — M (microfold) cells overlying Peyer's patches have a basal pocket harboring lymphocytes and antigen-presenting cells, specialized for antigen sampling rather than absorption.
17Which feature distinguishes ileum from jejunum?
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — The prominent, numerous Peyer's patches are the classic histological hallmark distinguishing the ileum from the jejunum.
18Urogastrone secreted by intestinal glands:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Urogastrone (epidermal growth factor) inhibits gastric acid secretion and promotes mucosal healing.
19Which structure is retroperitoneal in part?
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — Most of the duodenum (apart from its first part) is secondarily retroperitoneal, fixed against the posterior abdominal wall.
20A biopsy shows abundant goblet cells, fewer villi, and large lymphoid aggregates opposite mesenteric attachment. Diagnosis?
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — Shorter/fewer villi, increased goblet cells, and large antimesenteric lymphoid aggregates (Peyer's patches) are characteristic of the ileum.
21The primary function of the large intestine is:
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — The large intestine has no villi and performs little digestion; its main job is absorbing water and electrolytes and forming/storing feces.
22Which of the following is NOT a part of the large intestine?
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — The jejunum is a segment of the small intestine, not the large intestine.
23The longitudinal muscle layer of the large intestine forms:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Unlike the small intestine, the outer longitudinal muscle of the colon is condensed into three thickened bands called the taeniae coli.
24The pouch-like structures in the large intestine is caused by:
✅ Show Answer
✅ D — The taeniae coli are shorter than the colon wall, causing it to pucker into sacculations called haustra.
25Vitamin K is mainly synthesized by:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Resident colonic bacterial flora synthesize vitamin K, supplementing dietary intake.
26The large intestine, in adults, is approximately?
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — The adult large intestine measures roughly 1.5 meters in length, much shorter than the small intestine.
27Which type of cells in the large intestine are primarily responsible for mucus secretion?
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — Goblet cells, which are especially numerous in the colon, secrete the mucus that lubricates the passage of increasingly solid fecal content.
28Which anatomical feature characterizes the muscularis externa of the large intestine?
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — The muscularis externa of the colon has an inner circular layer plus an outer longitudinal layer condensed into the three teniae coli.
29What is the primary role of the abundant bacterial flora present in the large intestine?
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Colonic bacteria mainly contribute by synthesizing vitamins (notably K and some B vitamins) rather than digestive enzymes.
30In the context of the appendix, which of the following statements is true?
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — The vermiform appendix is rich in lymphoid follicles in its mucosa and submucosa, giving it a tonsil-like appearance and earning it the nickname "abdominal tonsil."
31Paneth cells are located:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Paneth cells are found at the BASE of the crypts of Lieberkühn, where they secrete lysozyme and defensins.
32Which layer contains the myenteric plexus?
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — The myenteric (Auerbach's) plexus lies BETWEEN the inner circular and outer longitudinal layers of the muscularis externa.
33A histological section shows numerous goblet cells, Peyer's patches and short villi. This section is taken from:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Numerous goblet cells, prominent Peyer's patches, and shorter villi are characteristic of the ILEUM.
34Which feature best distinguishes the jejunum from the duodenum histologically?
✅ Show Answer
✅ D — Both jejunum and duodenum have villi, crypts, and enterocytes, but Brunner's glands (in the submucosa) are unique to the DUODENUM and ABSENT in the jejunum.
35Compared with the small intestine, the large intestine contains:
✅ Show Answer
✅ D — The large intestine has NO villi, NO Paneth cells, and NO Brunner's glands, but it has MORE goblet cells than the small intestine.
36Which feature helps distinguish the large intestine from the small intestine histologically?
✅ Show Answer
✅ D — Both share simple columnar epithelium, crypts, and lamina propria, but only the large intestine completely LACKS VILLI — the key distinguishing feature.
37Which cell type is most numerous in the surface epithelium of the large intestine?
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Goblet cells are the most numerous cell type in the large intestine's surface epithelium, increasing in number toward the sigmoid colon.
38The secretory units of the exocrine portion of the pancreas are:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — The exocrine pancreas is a purely SEROUS gland; its secretory units are serous acini. Islets of Langerhans are the endocrine portion, not secretory units of the exocrine gland.
39Which feature distinguishes the exocrine portion of the pancreas from the parotid gland histologically?
✅ Show Answer
✅ D — Both pancreas and parotid have serous acini, septa, and resemble each other closely, but CENTROACINAR CELLS are unique to the pancreas and absent in the parotid.
40A histological section shows dark staining serous acini, centroacinar cells and pale staining islets. This section is taken from:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Centroacinar cells plus pale-staining islets surrounded by dark serous acini are diagnostic of the PANCREAS.
41The functional unit of the liver which is classically hexagonal in shape is:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — The classical hepatic lobule is the hexagonal functional unit, centered on a central vein with portal triads at its corners.
42Kupffer cells are:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Kupffer cells are resident macrophages lining the hepatic sinusoids, responsible for phagocytosis of bacteria and debris.
43Ito cells are responsible for:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Ito (hepatic stellate) cells, located in the Space of Disse, store Vitamin A and can transform into collagen-producing myofibroblasts in liver injury.
44Sinusoids differ from capillaries because they:
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — Hepatic sinusoids are lined by discontinuous, fenestrated endothelium with a discontinuous/absent basement membrane, allowing free exchange of plasma with hepatocytes.
45A patient has Vitamin A deficiency due to liver failure. Which liver cell normally stores Vitamin A?
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — Ito cells (hepatic stellate cells) in the Space of Disse are the dedicated storage site for Vitamin A in the liver.
46Hepatocytes are arranged in:
✅ Show Answer
✅ A — Hepatocytes are arranged in branching, anastomosing PLATES (cords) one to two cells thick, separated by sinusoids.
47The hepatic acinus is primarily based on:
✅ Show Answer
✅ A — The hepatic acinus (Rappaport's functional unit) is organized around the terminal branches of the hepatic artery/portal vein, defining zones by their BLOOD FLOW (oxygenation) gradient.
48Centroacinar cells are:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Centroacinar cells are pale, low cuboidal/squamous cells forming the intra-acinar portion of the intercalated duct — a feature unique to the pancreas.
49Which duct is absent in the pancreas?
✅ Show Answer
✅ D — Unlike the parotid gland, the pancreas LACKS striated ducts; its duct system is centroacinar → intercalated → intralobular → interlobular → main duct.
50The zymogen granules of pancreatic acinar cells are located in the:
✅ Show Answer
✅ D — Zymogen granules, containing inactive proenzymes, are concentrated in the APICAL cytoplasm of pancreatic acinar cells, giving it an acidophilic appearance.
51Basophilia of pancreatic acinar cells is mainly due to:
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — The BASAL basophilia of acinar cells results from abundant ROUGH endoplasmic reticulum (RER), which synthesizes digestive enzyme precursors.
52Which enzyme is secreted by the exocrine pancreas?
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — Trypsinogen is an exocrine secretory product of pancreatic acinar cells. Insulin, glucagon, and somatostatin are endocrine hormones from the islets of Langerhans.
53Which of the following is not a feature of the exocrine pancreas?
✅ Show Answer
✅ C — Striated ducts are a feature of salivary glands (e.g., parotid) but are ABSENT in the exocrine pancreas.
54The pancreas is considered as:
✅ Show Answer
✅ A — The exocrine pancreas is classified as a compound SEROUS tubuloacinar gland, histologically resembling the parotid gland.
55The space of Disse is located between:
✅ Show Answer
✅ A — The Space of Disse is the perisinusoidal space located between the hepatocyte surface and the sinusoidal endothelium, allowing plasma exchange.
56The direction of blood flow in the liver is:
✅ Show Answer
✅ A — Blood flows from the portal triad (portal vein + hepatic artery branches) through the sinusoids TOWARD the central vein.
57The direction of bile flow in the liver is:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Bile flows in the OPPOSITE direction to blood — from hepatocytes via bile canaliculi toward the portal triad (bile ductules), i.e., from central vein region to portal triad.
58A toxic drug causes damage to macrophages in liver sinusoids. Which function will be impaired?
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Kupffer cells are the macrophages of the liver sinusoids; their damage impairs PHAGOCYTOSIS of bacteria and debris, not bile production, glycogen storage, or albumin synthesis (all hepatocyte functions).
59A patient has jaundice due to obstruction of bile flow. Bile normally flows:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Bile normally flows from hepatocytes into bile canaliculi, then toward the bile ductules at the PORTAL TRIAD, opposite to the direction of blood flow.
60Studying the hepatic acinus, oxygen concentration is highest near:
✅ Show Answer
✅ B — Oxygen-rich blood enters at the portal triad (Zone 1 of the hepatic acinus), making oxygen concentration HIGHEST there and progressively lower toward Zone 3 near the central vein.

1. Histological Structure of Hepatocytes (Important)

Hepatocyte
LM
ArrangementAnastomosing cords (plates); radiate from central vein; blood sinusoids and Kupffer cells between hepatocytes
ShapePolyhedral; has 6 or more surfaces
NucleusSingle, central, rounded nucleus; about 25% of hepatocytes is binucleated
CytoplasmAcidophilic cytoplasm; stained by PAS, Best's carmine demonstrated by glycogen in cell
EM
NucleusCentral euchromatic; peripheral heterochromatic; one or two nucleoli
Cytoplasm Well-developed SER: for detoxification of drugs
Abundant RER: protein synthesis, plasma proteins
Numerous mitochondria: for energy production
Well-developed Golgi
Free ribosome: for protein formation
Peroxisome to detoxify (H₂O₂, alcohol, lipid)
Lysosome to digest and eliminate foreign bodies
Intermediate filaments: cytokeratin and thin actin filament
Cell inclusions: lipid droplets and glycogen granules
Cell membrane — Each cell surfaceIn contact with other hepatocytes
In contact with blood sinusoid wall through space of Disse
Microvilli at both sinusoidal and bile surfaces
Cell membrane — In-between cellsJunctional complexes
Plasma membrane shows indentation and projections, hold cells together
Each two adjacent cells share in the formation of bile canaliculi
